stem:
Priya switches on the electric room heater at her home in Jaipur. After a few minutes, the nichrome coil inside the heater becomes warm and glows.
Why does the nichrome coil become warm when the heater is switched on?

options.text: The coil becomes warm simply because the switch is connected to the mains supply.
Current flows through the coil, the resistance of nichrome opposes the current, and heat is produced.
The coil becomes warm first, and its warmth then makes the electric current flow.
Only nichrome wires become warm; the current passes through them without any resistance.

teacher.key_rationale: Heating is caused by current flowing against the resistance of the nichrome coil, converting electrical energy to heat; B states this causal chain correctly. A omits the role of resistance, C reverses cause and effect, and D falsely claims nichrome has no resistance.
